title: Build courses on first use, not all 66 at Courses.<clinit>
body:
## Summary
Courses.all baked 66 courses (spline, obstacles, branch alternatives, junctions) at class load although 38 are playable and one is raced.

## Description
Courses.all and Courses.playable become index-stable AbstractLists whose elements are built on first access (synchronized slot array). Courses.json is generated from the tables, byte-identical to Course.json. Courses.id/indexOf let Career answer id lookups without building anything.

## Flow
RaceGame start -> Courses.playableIndices (ids only) -> course(i) builds one course when the World is made.

## Expected impact
Time to first World drops by ~250 ms on desktop (est. 1.5-2.5 s on a Stick); every other course costs ~4-20 ms only if selected.

## Evaluation
- Claim: Courses.all init cost falls by >90% with no behaviour change
- Before: Courses.all (66) 271-308 ms
- After: 21-24 ms (first World pays its own ~21 ms)
- Method: StartupBench (cold JVM, JDK 22, phases timed with nanoTime, 3-4 runs)
- Result: better, -250 ms
- Gate: LazyCoursesTest (json byte-identical, identity, index map) + full gates
evidence: core/Tracks.kt Courses, Career.kt, AshCircuit.kt; commit baf5181a

title: Single-pass CSV table parser
body:
## Summary
Content.table built readLines + filter + drop + zip().toMap() per row.

## Description
One pass with a hand split into LinkedHashMap; same maps, same key order, same fatal errors. An oracle test parses every CSV under data/ with the legacy parser and compares maps and key order.

## Flow
Every Content.table call at load.

## Expected impact
~15% off cold startup phases (CarCatalog first touch 57 -> 42 ms).

## Evaluation
- Claim: Faster parse with identical output
- Before: startup phases total 385-440 ms (after lazy courses)
- After: 326-340 ms
- Method: StartupBench (cold JVM, JDK 22, phases timed with nanoTime, 3-4 runs)
- Result: better, modest
- Gate: ContentParseTest oracle over all tables + full gates

title: Coarse-to-fine projection bins (10 m) with exact argmin
body:
## Summary
Course.project scanned ~260 candidate segments per call and was 50% of sim step time; the first projection of a course baked bins in 40-110 ms (the Stick startup stall).

## Description
Bins are built 80 m -> 40 -> 20 -> 10 m, each child filtering its parent's list (a segment that cannot be nearest anywhere in the parent cannot be nearest in the child). The nearest segment is exactly what the 20 m grid returned. Bake is 8-14 ms.

## Flow
First project() -> bakeCandidates (lazy) -> hot loop walks ~100 not ~260 candidates.

## Expected impact
Sim step -39% on desktop; bake 5-8x faster (est. 0.3-0.7 s saved on Stick at course select). Memory: ~0.7M ints per baked course (2.8 MB) vs 0.3M.

## Evaluation
- Claim: Same projection result, fewer candidates
- Before: SimBench mean 76-79 us/step; bake 40-110 ms
- After: 46.9 us/step; bake 8-14 ms
- Method: SimBench (7 playable courses, six classed AI cars, Pro skill, combat on, 6000 steps x best of 5 in-process, median of 3-5 fresh JVMs, JDK 22); ProjectionProbe for bins/bake
- Result: better
- Gate: ProjectionBinsTest: bit-equal to an exhaustive scan over 6,000 random in-bounds points; SimBench GOLDEN and CollisionGolden (5 contact-heavy replays, ~3,700 contact steps, recorded on the parent commit) bit-identical; :core:test, :link:test, :game:test, :app:assembleDebug green

title: Cache each car's heading cos/sin
body:
## Summary
StrictTrig.cos was 19% of sim time: collide evaluates cos/sin(heading) 36 times per pair, three solver passes, plus contain/obstacles/combat.

## Description
Car.cosHeading/sinHeading recompute only when the heading bits change; every value is the identical StrictTrig result. 27 call sites switched.

## Flow
heading integrates once per step -> all later reads hit the cache.

## Expected impact
Sim step -37%.

## Evaluation
- Claim: Same values, far fewer StrictTrig calls
- Before: 46 us/step
- After: 28.8 us/step
- Method: SimBench (7 playable courses, six classed AI cars, Pro skill, combat on, 6000 steps x best of 5 in-process, median of 3-5 fresh JVMs, JDK 22)
- Result: better
- Gate: SimBench GOLDEN and CollisionGolden (5 contact-heavy replays, ~3,700 contact steps, recorded on the parent commit) bit-identical; :core:test, :link:test, :game:test, :app:assembleDebug green
evidence: core/World.kt Car, Combat.kt, Obstacles.kt, Abilities.kt, Drift.kt, AiBehaviour.kt; commit 0505a43a

title: Replay contain()'s projection on bit-equal inputs
body:
## Summary
contain() runs 4x per step (once and after each of three solver passes) and projects two end points per car; most repeats have identical inputs.

## Description
Per car end, remember (x,y,hint,route) bits and the projection; a bit-equal repeat copies the stored answer. Course.project is pure on an immutable course so the result is identical by construction.

## Flow
step -> contain x4 -> projectEnd -> hit/miss.

## Expected impact
Sim step -20%.

## Evaluation
- Claim: Same results, ~half the contain projections
- Before: 28.8 us/step
- After: 23.2 us/step
- Method: SimBench (7 playable courses, six classed AI cars, Pro skill, combat on, 6000 steps x best of 5 in-process, median of 3-5 fresh JVMs, JDK 22)
- Result: better
- Gate: SimBench GOLDEN and CollisionGolden (5 contact-heavy replays, ~3,700 contact steps, recorded on the parent commit) bit-identical; :core:test, :link:test, :game:test, :app:assembleDebug green

title: Distance-sorted bin lists with a lower-bound early exit
body:
## Summary
Course.distance2 is still ~35-39% of the sim step after the bin change.

## Description
Store each bin sorted by centre distance with a parallel float distance, and stop once centre distance - half-diagonal exceeds the best so far (break only for in-bin points; ties by lowest index; junction pass needs the index tie-break). Expect distance2 work 100 -> ~15 candidates, est. sim -25%, +30% bin memory.

## Flow
Course.project hot loop and bake.

## Expected impact
Est. -4 us/step desktop (~-30 us on a Stick). The whole sim step is ~17 us desktop, so this is 1% of a 16.7 ms frame on device: low priority.

## Evaluation
- Claim: Early exit returns the same argmin
- Before: 16.55 us/step
- After: unbuilt; est 12 us/step
- Method: ProjectionBinsTest oracle would be the gate; needs a junction-course oracle too
- Result: unbuilt
- Gate: needs ProjectionBinsTest extended to junction/branch courses

title: Link: RaceServer 'track' message and routesJson force every course to build
body:
## Summary
RaceServer.kt:223 does Courses.all.indexOfFirst{id} and :280 joins Courses.all; with lazy slots these build up to 66 courses (an ~270 ms desktop hitch, seconds on a Stick) on the first track change / routes request.

## Description
Use Courses.indexOf(id) for the id lookup and iterate Courses.playable (or table metadata) for routesJson. RaceGame.kt:18 'Courses.all+trackPreview.course' copies the whole list only in preview mode. Outside core's write set.

## Flow
Controller track pick -> RaceServer -> Courses.

## Expected impact
Removes a first-use hitch that this round's laziness would otherwise move to the controller path.

## Evaluation
- Claim: No course builds on a track pick
- Before: not measured (stream L)
- After: unbuilt
- Method: Time the 'track' message on desktop with the lazy list
- Result: unbuilt
- Gate: link tests

title: First-race frame hitch of ~1.1 s on the Stick (lobby to race transition)
body:
## Summary
Frame time max 1139-1145 ms once per race start on the Stick, unchanged after lazy courses and off-thread bake.

## Description
Stick /stats frameTimeMs.sinceStart.max 1,145 ms in two runs (before and after the drain wave); p95 18.3 ms. The course bake moved off the render thread (e13d7cef) and did not remove it, so the cause is elsewhere in the lobby-to-race switch: scenery canvas bake, region material/texture load (AtlasArt.selectRegion), first-use shader or atlas page upload.

## Flow
- start race from lobby
- log per-phase timestamps around selectRegion, sceneryBake and first draw with the FrameProfiler
- move the slow phase to the lobby or the countdown

## Expected impact
Removes one visible 1 s freeze at every race start.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - no frame over 100 ms at race start
Before: max 1139-1145 ms on the Stick (2 runs)
After: P9 attributed it to the first course.project() of each course building its lazy bins on the render thread (1,138.5-2,268.3 ms per first visit). P10 bakes them on a course worker before the pick is queued: render-thread first project() 0.034-0.389 ms on every first visit, bin wait 0 in 24 of 24 bakes, no render over 100 ms in the bake phase; transition max 2,376.9 (P9) -> 245.8-374.4 ms over four 360 s Stick runs. selectRegion on a switch 61.4-117.1 -> 5.8-16.5 ms (0ed2537e).
Method: probe - perf-device --profile --warm-routes --tracks (five themes), twice per APK, tools/perf-p10.py
Result: better - the ~1.1-2.3 s freeze is gone. The card's 100 ms bar still fails (41-43 transition windows over 100 ms per run): render-thread profile saves, 50-156 ms each at car picks and race start/finish, split into its own card (operator: money/data path)
Gate: :core:test :link:test :game:test; CoursePrewarmTest (bit-identical projection), TrackRequestTest
evidence: commits d3c68fec (bins off the render thread), 0ed2537e (region tiles prepared off it), 59f5605e (a pick lands before a queued start); docs/concepts/deathride/P10-race-start-hitch.md; deathride/evidence/perf/p10/

title: Render-thread profile saves: 50-156 ms per save at car picks, race start and finish on the Stick
body:
## Summary
After P10 the only lobby-to-race frames over 100 ms are profile saves on the render thread: ProfileStore.save 49.5-156.1 ms each, plus its garage publish 8.2-58.3 ms.

## Description
RaceGame.editProfile runs ProfileStore.save (encode, decode-verify, write a temporary file with fd.sync(), read and verify the old save, copy it to a backup, atomic move) on the render thread. A car pick is one save (70.0-168.5 ms request), startRace is two (144.5-366.5 ms), finishRace is two inside the sim block (231.6 ms seen). P9's diagnostic APK already showed 159-336 ms requests-phase frames on every switch.

## Flow
phone car/start or race finish -> RaceGame.editProfile -> ProfileStore.save -> Garage/Career publish

## Expected impact
Removes the remaining 150-370 ms transition frames (41-43 windows over 100 ms per 360 s run).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - no transition frame over 100 ms
Before: transition max 245.8-374.4 ms (P10, four runs)
After: unbuilt
Method: probe - perf-device --profile --warm-routes --tracks, tools/perf-p10.py
Result: unbuilt - money/data path: the Economy.start ticket and settled cash depend on the save completing; moving it to a writer thread changes when a save is known to have happened, which is an owner decision
Gate: profile/economy tests plus a Stick run
